support_mike: Customer CS-9421 hitting 400 when calling the file_uploader tool. Error from tool-runner: \"MalformedToolArgs: Unexpected token '\\' in JSON at position 15\". They say it worked locally for them. Need triage and a short customer-facing fix.

Alyssa (Support): Can you paste the exact request body and headers we received? Also did they use our SDK or raw HTTP?

support_mike: They were using our web UI (custom integration on their side) that posts multipart/form-data. Here's the anonymized raw multipart body we captured:

```
POST /v1/call_tool HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----BOUNDARY\r\n\r\n------BOUNDARY\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"tool_args\"\r\n\r\n"{'file_path':'C:\\Users\\ACME\\invoices\\123.pdf', 'comment': 'scanned
on 2026-03-01'},"\r\n\r\n------BOUNDARY--\r\n```

Note: the tool_args value is double-quoted as a whole, then contains single quotes, unescaped backslashes and an embedded newline. That all lands at the server as one string, and our JSON parser chokes.

Ben S: Two separate problems here: (1) single quotes are not valid JSON (2) trailing comma after the object can cause some parsers to error (we do strict parse). More subtly, wrapping the JSON value in an outer quoted string (\"...\") means the server receives a JSON string whose contents are a non-JSON snippet. I also saw in logs that node-sdk v0.9 had a multipart codepath that serializes tool_args as a literal string and wraps it in quotes when using form-data, which can double-encode. Our parser error \"Unexpected token '\\'\" indicates the backslashes (Windows paths) weren't escaped correctly inside that quoted string.

support_mike: Raw capture from inbound bytes (showing exact quotes/backslashes):

```
------BOUNDARY\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"tool_args\"\r\n\r\n"{'file_path':'C:\\Users\\ACME\\invoices\\123.pdf', 'comment': 'scanned
on 2026-03-01'}"\r\n------BOUNDARY--\r\n```

Alyssa (Support): Oof. Looks like the integrator pasted a Python dict into the form field (single quotes + unescaped backslashes + embedded newline), then their client wrapped it in an extra pair of quotes. That exact combo will fail strict JSON parse.

Ben S: Short-term: update our error to be more actionable. Instead of generic \"MalformedToolArgs\" return, include a hint when we detect outer-quoted values or single-quote usage: e.g., \"tool_args looks like a quoted/non-JSON payload (single quotes or trailing comma). Please provide valid JSON (double quotes) or use SDK v1.x which handles multipart serializing.\"

Ben S: Long-term: I propose adding a tolerant preflight step on the multipart codepath that tries the following heuristics before failing: (a) if the value is an outer-quoted string, unquote once and try parse; (b) if parse fails but the payload contains only single quotes and matching braces, try a safe convert (single -> double quotes) with strict validation; (c) reject if suspicious control chars (\u0000, BEL, vertical tab) are present. We should log when we auto-correct and include an audit flag.

Alyssa (Support): For the customer reply, I'll give repro + fix. Proposed reply (I'll send after you sanity-check):

```
Thanks for the report — root cause is that the tool_args field you sent is not valid JSON. It looks like a Python-style dict wrapped in an extra quote, e.g. \"{'file_path': 'C:\\\\Users\\\\ACME\\\\invoices\\\\123.pdf', ... }\".

Please send tool_args as valid JSON (double quotes, escaped backslashes), for example (curl):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call_tool \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"tool": "upload_file", "tool_args": {"file_path": "C:\\\\Users\\\\ACME\\\\invoices\\\\123.pdf", "comment": "scanned on 2026-03-01"}}'

Or if you must use multipart/form-data, make sure the form field contains raw JSON (no surrounding quotes) and that backslashes are escaped. If you used our Node SDK please upgrade to v1.x; v0.9 has a multipart bug that double-quotes tool_args in certain flows.

If you'd like, paste the exact body and we can sanitize it for you.
```

support_mike: I'll send that. Customer replied saying they were indeed pasting a Python dict into a small admin tool. They said they can change it.

Maria (QA): I'll add a regression test for multipart/form-data that covers these cases:
- outer-quoted tool_args (\"...\") containing single-quoted dict
- windows paths with backslashes
- embedded CRLF or LF in values
- trailing comma after object

sre-bot: Logged incident CS-9421 -> ticket updated.

Alyssa (Support): Closing loop: customer accepted the fix and updated their integration. We should still do the SDK fix + better error message as Ben suggested.

support_mike: Thanks — moving to done and adding engineering task for tolerant preflight + SDK patch. :thumbsup:
